root_cause.text: The GRO completion stage did not clear the `encapsulation` flag that could be set by hardware NICs, the tun driver, or veth setups, causing `udp4_gro_complete()` to use the inner network offset instead of the outer network offset when computing the UDP pseudo checksum.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `skb->encapsulation = 0;` at the beginning of the `gro_complete()` function with the comment "NICs can feed encapsulated packets into GRO". The CVE description explicitly states that "udp4_gro_complete() uses the wrong network offset (inner instead of outer) to compute the outer UDP header pseudo checksum" when the encapsulation flag is not cleared, and that hardware NICs, the tun driver, and veth setups can all set this flag on incoming packets, violating the implicit assumption that the flag would be zeroed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear the encapsulation flag on socket buffers during GRO completion to prevent mishandling of encapsulated packets in protocol callbacks.
intent_record.what: Added a comment and a statement that sets skb->encapsulation to 0 before the rcu_read_lock() call in the gro_complete function.
intent_record.how: This change clears the encapsulation flag on the socket buffer before processing GRO completion callbacks. This ensures that encapsulated packets are treated as non-encapsulated during the GRO completion phase, preventing incorrect handling of nested packet structures in the protocol type callbacks.
